children.description:
Objective: make the existing production PHP and Schedule convergence paths establish the traversal required by Schedule scripts through the shared /etc/orbit parent, without broadening protected sibling access.

Scope: apps/gateway/app/Infrastructure/AppInstances/RemoteProductionPhpRuntimeManager.php; app/Infrastructure/Schedules/RemoteScheduleRuntimeManager.php; app/Infrastructure/Doctor/NativeScheduleStateInspector.php; only directly needed narrow supporting Gateway code; focused Gateway regressions; affected lines in docs/reference/php-runtime.md and docs/reference/schedules.md. Keep the existing Schedule permission issue code and bounded report shape. Do not introduce CLI/SDK changes, a generic filesystem framework, dependencies, harness changes, a fleet sweep, recursive chmod/chown, new ADRs, or a new lifecycle operation. In particular /etc/orbit/php-fpm mode 0700 is evidence, not a request to make that subtree traversable by applications.

Confirmed diagnosis: on ORB-71's disposable Ubuntu 26.04 app-prod Node, install is uutils coreutils 0.8.0. Real root-owned /etc/orbit and /etc/orbit/php-fpm are 0700, /etc/orbit/schedules is 0755, and the protected script was root:orbit-app-1 0750. namei found no symlinks; getfacl showed no extended ACLs. systemd could not spawn the script and returned 203/EXEC. The owner retained this evidence and yielded blocked; this task may not write its worktree or use its topology. RemoteProductionPhpRuntimeManager runs umask 0077 before install -d ...0755 on /etc/orbit/php-fpm/<user> and validates only that final directory. uutils 0.8.0 creates missing ancestors using create_dir_all and chmods the final operand. Schedule installation likewise configures only its child directories, and the current Doctor permissions probe checks leaves rather than runtime traversal. This explains the current failure mechanism; the exact historical first creator is not proved. Snapshot refresh is not a product fix.

Implementation choices remain open inside that contract: choose the smallest safe parent mode and narrow code reuse. Reject conflicting ownership, symlinks, and non-directories before changing the target or descendants. Supported convergence repairs a real root:root 0700 parent; no manual chmod is acceptance. Preserve private umask for protected material, effective sibling access restrictions, operator tuning bytes, unrelated service/user identity, and the current script ownership/isolation and non-blocking run semantics. Do not inspect real secret contents; use non-secret fixture sentinels and access/metadata checks. Schedule Doctor remains strictly read-only and reuses schedule.artifact_permissions_mismatch; no new public code, CLI, or SDK cutover is needed.

Verification: run the required Gateway guidance check before edits, then extend existing ProductionPhpRuntimeTest.php, RemoteScheduleRuntimeManagerTest.php and ScheduleDoctorProbeTest.php (or the nearest native-inspector test) with executable behavior/failure coverage. Tests to add include missing/shared-parent creation, existing root:root 0700 convergence, retries/order, all three conflicts, protected sibling/tuning/service preservation and read-only ancestor detection. Tests named here are planned additions, not claimed results. Run meaningful unfiltered composer test:affected from apps/gateway and composer check there, plus root composer docs-lint and git diff --check. Never pass Pest a path/filter/group/suite; a zero-selected TIA run is not acceptance. Keep caller Commander database, cache, and providers out of project checks, and use only safe disposable project test configuration.

Incus execution after authorized admission: discovery is the planned flow; incus does not select proof. Acquire a new issue-owned topology through existing bin/e2e-topology machinery after preparation review. Read apps/e2e/AGENTS.md and docs/reference/incus-topologies.md before acquisition; inspect the restored baseline and available product state. Never access ORB-71's machines or worktree. Await each topology command before the next, across all Nodes, and obey the exclusive command lock. Use focused executable disposable fixtures for the conflict matrix and convergence/order regressions. Required real-machine checks establish actual production execution, intended/unrelated-user access, protected sibling preservation, and read-only Doctor before/after supported convergence. Add further Incus cases only for an identified OS uncertainty; do not inventory unrelated services. Do not erase an existing shared directory to simulate a missing one: choose a clean disposable setup or preserve and restore the exact fixture with recorded ownership. Use supported Gateway API or the existing typed PHP SDK to provision a production target, install a stopped Schedule, select its first release, request a run, and observe actual completion plus a unique non-secret journal marker while the timer stays disabled. No ORB-71 CLI command is a prerequisite. Verify another unprivileged account cannot read or replace the script and that protected sibling sentinels remain inaccessible. Record exact setup and cleanup; harness repair is separately owned. Report 'Discovery development only; isolated acceptance proof not run'.

Handoff: provide reviewable uncommitted changes with C1-C6 mapped to exact commands, cwd/topology/Node, observed result and exit status, retained logs, setup failures/corrections, and temporary changes with cleanup or remaining state. Use the assignment-bound native receipt and yield; the same implementer handles corrections. Only the assigned reviewer creates the single clean sole-parent commit after snapshot review. issue.title: Preserve runtime traversal through the shared Orbit directory
issue.description:
Production Schedules can execute their protected scripts after Gateway production PHP runtime or Schedule convergence, within the [existing Schedule contract](<https://github.com/nckrtl/orbit/blob/main/docs/decisions/0013-native-systemd-schedule-management.md>). On the disposable Ubuntu 26.04 production Node used with source `fb5bcd9fd752c5c3eb59699b26616d73d4b7c420`, installation succeeded but execution failed with `203/EXEC` because `/etc/orbit` was `root:root 0700`; the responsible Gateway code remains on current main `cf3f4d7e9ae316c4699d61e7da366b7623196809`.

## Scope

* In: Gateway production PHP runtime and Schedule shared-parent convergence, their focused regression tests, and the existing verify-only Schedule permission probe.
* In: The affected operational lines in the PHP runtime and Schedule references.
* Out: CLI or SDK changes, harness changes, dependency changes, fleet repair, or a general permission framework.
* Out: Broader access to `/etc/orbit/php-fpm` or other protected siblings, recursive permission changes, new Schedule lifecycle behavior, or new architecture.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Production PHP runtime convergence and Schedule installation establish runtime traversal through `/etc/orbit` when it is missing or is an existing real `root:root` directory with mode `0700`, including PHP-first and Schedule-first creation and repeated convergence. Proof: focused cases added to Gateway `ProductionPhpRuntimeTest.php` and `RemoteScheduleRuntimeManagerTest.php`, plus Incus discovery with the supported guest `install` implementation.
- [ ] A foreign-owned, symlinked, or non-directory `/etc/orbit` is refused without adopting, replacing, deleting, or changing that object or its contents. Proof: focused executable Gateway tests using disposable fixtures for each conflict.
- [ ] Parent convergence preserves protected sibling contents and access restrictions, PHP operator tuning, unrelated users and services, credentials, and per-Schedule script isolation. Proof: Gateway preservation regressions and Incus discovery checks of scoped fixture metadata, tuning fingerprints, service identity, and access by the intended and unrelated users.
- [ ] After supported production setup and Schedule installation, a manual run completes as the derived production user with the expected journal marker while its timer remains disabled. Proof: an Incus discovery observation through existing Gateway API or PHP SDK operations, followed by bounded service-completion and journal checks; a successful non-blocking start request alone does not pass.
- [ ] Schedule Doctor reports the existing bounded artifact-permissions mismatch when an ancestor prevents the derived runtime user reaching an otherwise valid script, and reports no such mismatch after supported convergence; inspection makes no host changes and exposes no sensitive diagnostics. Proof: focused native-inspector and Schedule Doctor regressions plus read-only Incus discovery observations before and after convergence.
- [ ] Operational references explain shared-parent traversal, the supported convergence recovery boundary, preservation of protected contents, and the Schedule Doctor permission check. Proof: review of the affected lines in `docs/reference/php-runtime.md` and `docs/reference/schedules.md`, followed by `composer docs-lint`.
